local.project: 121/121 pass on the pinned tree, with the reference fix and with every pass/hardening patch

traps.shape: the request manager's redirect loop replays the caller's request headers to the redirect target with no origin comparison; the target receives the credential
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the redirect is followed by the same client for the same caller, so replaying the request headers looks like what keeps an authenticated chain working
traps.realistic_because: published fix site for GHSA-www2-v7xj-xrc6 (CVE-2018-20060, commit 560bd227) and the surface the report's example hits

traps.shape: the same redirect loop must withhold every credential header the caller attached, not only the one the report's example carries; the rule also applies to credentials configured on the client rather than passed on the call, and on every hop of a chain
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the published advisory and the report's example name only the Authorization header, so a fix that removes that one header reads as complete
traps.realistic_because: the same class of credential the package withheld later (the 2023 follow-up advisory added Cookie to the removal set); the value travels the same guarded path but the report never names it

traps.shape: what counts as another origin: a same-host redirect to a different port leaves the origin, while a relative Location or a differently-cased host name stays on it; a host-only or raw-string comparison keeps the credential on the port change
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the Location is joined to an absolute URL before any guard runs and most redirects keep the scheme, so comparing the parsed host (or the raw URL string) looks sufficient and the port or case shapes look like edge cases
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the package's own host comparison normalises default ports, but the redirect guard does not exist at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the connection pool's own redirect loop, reachable whenever a pool is used to reach foreign hosts (assert_same_host=False), re-sends the caller's headers to the redirect target without any origin comparison
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the pool is single-host by design: assert_same_host defaults to True and raises HostChangedError, so a cross-host redirect looks unreachable and the documented proxy use of the pool looks like an edge case the manager handles
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the pool's redirect loop is untouched by both published fixes

traps.shape: the URLFetch-backed manager lets the platform follow redirects, so the headers are replayed to every hop without the library seeing them; the redirect has to be followed in the manager for the origin to be checked
traps.reason_to_dismiss: URLFetch follows redirects inside the platform, the manager is legacy platform-specific contrib code, and the library cannot see intermediate hops without disabling the platform's redirect handling
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: a second redirect-following implementation in the package, untouched by both published fixes

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (written after the build), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the property governs where a request goes, not access to a resource; there is no neighbouring object to authorise
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: redirect following has no roles and no per-direction variants; every hop runs the same code
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the guarded path is redirect following, not reads versus writes; no verb distinction exists
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no attacker-supplied value is normalised or adjusted before the guard; the Location is compared as delivered
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority, role or secret lookup takes part in this decision

A.summary: Authorization header not removed on a cross-origin redirect

B.summary: Authorization header still forwarded on a cross-origin redirect when the header name is spelled in another case (incomplete fix of CVE-2018-20060)
